cases.name: 01-exact-quote
cases.why: A quote copied verbatim, with every number present in it, is the baseline the gate exists to admit.

cases.name: 02-paraphrased-quote
cases.why: A model that rewrites the span instead of copying it must be dropped: a paraphrase cannot be checked against the source.

cases.name: 03-number-absent-from-quote
cases.why: A real quote attached to an invented figure is the most dangerous shape: the quote verifies, the number does not appear in it.

cases.name: 04-thousands-separator
cases.why: Sources write 1,024 and models write 1024. Normalisation must treat them as the same number, or honest claims are lost.

cases.name: 05-smart-quotes
cases.why: Typeset sources use curly quotes; models emit straight ones. The comparison must not fail on punctuation the author never chose.

cases.name: 06-dangling-fragment
cases.why: A span cut mid-clause is not evidence of anything; the claim it supports cannot be checked against a sentence that never ends.

cases.name: 07-quote-too-short
cases.why: A span short enough to occur by chance proves nothing, so it is refused before it can ground a claim.

cases.name: 08-invalid-type
cases.why: TYPE is a closed vocabulary. A value outside it means the model improvised the schema, which is not a record to trust.

cases.name: 09-invalid-strength
cases.why: STRENGTH carries the hedging. An unrecognised value would let a speculative result be written as settled fact.

cases.name: 10-hedged-claim-survives
cases.why: Hedged is a legitimate strength, not a defect. Dropping it would silently discard every limitation a paper states.

cases.name: 11-mixed-section
cases.why: A realistic section: several candidates, only some verifiable. This is the case that moves if extraction quality or gate strictness changes.

cases.name: 12-duplicate-claims
cases.why: Models restate the same fact in adjacent blocks. Both verify, so only de-duplication keeps the ledger honest about how much was found.
